To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
post‐hemodialytic dosing of 2 g vs. 1 g ceftzidime in an anuric ESDR patients resulted in similar pharmacodynamic outcomes and tolerability.
the post‐hemodialyzed 1‐g ceftazidine dose achieves the pharmacodynamic target in 100% of patients for both 48‐hour and 72‐hours interdialytic periods.
a single post‐hemodialytic dose of 1 g ceftazidme achieves >70% time above minimal inhibitory concentrations for 48 and 72 hour interdialysis periods in anuric hemodialysis patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the determination of the concentration of the drug concentration.
a new drug‐drug interaction between ceftazidine and avibactam that may be clinically relevant.
the development of an effective, cost‐efficient and convenient dosing regimen of ceftazdime in ESRD patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ceftazidimes post‐hemodialytic dosing is a viable option in the treatment of sepsis in anuric hemodialysis patients.
the 1‐gram dose of ceftazidine is safe and efficacious in the treatment of infections of end stage renal disease patients.
the 2 g dosing of ceftazdime in the anuric ESKD population is not necessary and may be replaced by a 1 g dose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 1 g post‐hemodialysate ceftazidim dose is sufficient to attain > 70% of the time‐concentration ratio of ceftazidine concentrations over the MIC of the pathogen.
ceftazidim is a safe and effective antimicrobial agent for the treatment of infections in ESRD patients.
the post‐hemodialytic administration of 1 g ceftzidime achieves a 48‐ and/or 72‐hour post‐dialytic exposure that is adequate for the treatment of most common Gram‐negative pathogens.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a 1‐g ceftazidine dose administered post‐hemodilysis in anuric dialysis patients achieves adequate pharmacodynamic exposure against common gram-negative pathogens associated with septicemia in ESRD patients.
1 g ceftaxidime post‐Hemodialysis is as effective as 2 g in anuric patients.
1 g ceftaxidime post‐HD is safe and effective in anuric hemodialysis patients.
